title: ACE I/D and AGT rs699 Polymorphisms and Positional Associations in Handball
content: The renin-angiotensin system (RAS) plays a central role in cardiovascular homeostasis and muscle physiology, and polymorphisms within key RAS genes — particularly angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) I/D and angiotensinogen (AGT) rs699 — have been widely studied in the context of athletic performance. Handball is a high-intensity team sport in which positional roles impose distinct physiological demands, yet position-specific genetic profiling remains underexplored. This study investigated the genotype and allele distributions of ACE I/D and AGT rs699 polymorphisms in 26 licensed elite male handball players and examined their associations with playing position. Genotyping was performed via conventional PCR (ACE I/D) and TaqMan real-time PCR (AGTrs699). Both polymorphisms were in Hardy–Weinberg equilibrium. A borderline association was identified between ACE I/D genotype and playing position across four positional categories (Fisher–Freeman–Halton exact test, p=0.047, Cramér's V=0.629), with the II genotype exclusively observed among goalkeepers and the DD genotype predominantly represented among pivot players; however, this association did not survive correction for multiple testing (Bonferroni-adjusted p=0.168; Benjamini–Hochberg q=0.136) and should be regarded as hypothesis-generating. In contrast, AGTrs699 genotype did not differ significantly across playing positions (χ²=6.035, p=0.419). These preliminary findings suggest that ACE I/D may contribute to positional differentiation in handball, whereas AGT rs699 appears insufficient to discriminate between positional roles within this athletically selected cohort. Larger, multi-site studies are needed to confirm these results.
